Hi Rohan / Monica,

Quick note from Aurora ops: our SREs just surfaced that two separate committed reservations appear to overlap on the same set of dedicated GPUs for July–Sept. We submitted a formal committed capacity request via your portal (attached commit statement) on Mar 30 and the renewal/expansion that our CS contact submitted on Apr 15 seems to have received a provisional allocation as well. We're concerned we'll end up double-counted or — worse — deprioritized if Redwood runs a first-commit-first-assign policy.

Can you confirm which commit is considered the authoritative one and whether we should expect any temporary throttling during the Jul ramp? Our timeline is tight: model evaluation starts Jul 8 and production traffic ramp targets Jul 20.

Thanks,

Thanks Rohan. Quick recap from Sales side:
- Mar 30 commit (DEAL-8721) = signed 12-month reserved pool (30 GPUs equivalent), executed and invoiced. This is the primary contract.
- Apr 15 intake was submitted as an "expansion request" tied to an integration pilot with a partner; no new signature or invoice processed yet. Intake ID: INT-4413.

I've attached a proposed allocation that minimizes disruption: keep the Mar 30 commit fully intact (as invoiced), and provision a provisional tranche of 6 GPUs from unallocated cloud buffer for the Apr 15 request through Sep 30, with a 14-day cancellation window if the partner pilot doesn't convert. If the pilot converts, we escalate to a formal amendment and move to permanent reserved instances.

Attachment: proposed_allocation.xlsx (see tab 'Aurora_proposal').

If Capacity agrees to the provisional tranche approach we can avoid carving into already-invoiced units and keep the ramp on schedule. If not, we should consider applying the prioritization matrix (SLA tier, invoiced commit, expansion pilot) and offer a service credit for delayed ramp.

- Monica

Rohan / Monica — quick position from Sales leadership: priority should be given to the invoiced, signed commitment. DEAL-8721 represents contractual obligation and revenue recognition — operationally we should not reassign those units unless the customer agrees.

Thanks everyone — decision and execution plan below.

Decision: prioritize the Mar 30 signed commit (DEAL-8721) — those 30 GPU-equivalents remain intact. For the Apr 15 expansion intake (INT-4413), Capacity will allocate a provisional tranche of 6 ephemeral GPUs out of the cloud buffer for Jul 8–Sep 30 with the following conditions:
- Trial tranche is provisional and will be reclaimed with 14 days notice if the partner pilot doesn't convert.
- Aurora receives one month of service credit if provisional tranche is reduced during their Jul ramp window.
- If the partner pilot converts, Sales will fast-track an amendment and Finance will convert provisional to reserved inventory on next replenishment cycle.

Action items:
- Monica: confirm amendment template and DocuSign path for provisional-to-reserved conversion by Mon 2027-04-26. (Owner: Monica)
- Marissa: schedule telemetry checks for Jul 8–Jul 22 to watch for throttling signals; notify Aurora SREs if throttling risk exceeds 5%. (Owner: Marissa)
- Capacity infra: mark 6 GPUs as provisional buffer units (internal ticket CAP-5932) and ensure routing policy prioritizes DEAL-8721 when load spikes. (Owner: Rohan)

Aurora / Jonas — we're committing to minimize disruption and will follow up with the DocuSign amendment link once Monica confirms. Appreciate your patience — please confirm acceptance of the provisional tranche and credit terms and we will start provisioning.

Rohan Mehta
